# Virtual Realty Assistants (VRA)

> VRA places trained, dedicated virtual assistants with businesses in any industry. Each assistant completes a mandatory 4-week,
> instructor-led training program before client work. Flat pricing: $1,500/month
> full-time (40 hrs/week) or $800/month part-time (20 hrs/week), both on a three-month commitment,
> no hidden fees, subject to applicable agreement terms. Check-ins at 14, 30, 60 and 90 days, with
> VA replacement at no extra cost. Founded in 2022 by Michael Bossart, a licensed Texas real estate
> broker who previously worked in title insurance as a county manager and as a residential agent.
> VRA began as a Keller Williams-centric company and has since expanded well beyond real estate.
> Based out of Keller Williams Memorial, Houston, TX.
> Contact: contact@vrealtyassistants.com

## What assistants do
- Administrative and office support: scheduling, calendar and inbox management, data entry, document organization, CRM and database upkeep, event and training coordination.
- Billing and receivables: preparing and sending invoices, calling on the client's own past-due invoices, working an aging report, logging promise-to-pay notes and escalating what needs the owner.
- Bids, quotes and proposals: preparing them from the client's templates and pricing, then following up until there is a decision.
- Each assistant completes the Essential Toolkit before their first client interview: Claude and ChatGPT, Canva, a brand-agnostic CRM, Zapier and Asana. Further training is available to deepen a skill a client's business needs, so it is not claimed that every assistant has every specialty.
- Process documentation: recording how the work is actually done, exceptions included, and writing it up as standard operating procedures (SOPs) the business owns — checklists, templates and step-by-step documents kept current as the process changes. VRA runs a training class specifically on identifying business processes and documenting them, including treating an SOP as a living document that is updated when the process changes rather than written once.
- Client and customer communication: phone and inbox coverage during the client's business hours, follow-up, review requests and responses.
- Sales support: outbound calling and appointment setting from the client's lead lists, speed-to-lead follow-up, pipeline reporting.
- Marketing support: social content and scheduling, email campaigns, Canva-certified graphic design.
- Website work: building a business website and the social accounts alongside it, finishing a site the client started but never completed (broken links, unbuilt service pages, missing content), writing and adding page content such as service pages and FAQs, design research on color and imagery delivered as a written recommendation, and keeping the site current as the business changes. Work requiring a developer stays with a developer.
- Recruiting and hiring coordination for the client's own hiring: job postings, applicant tracking, interview scheduling. Hiring decisions stay with the client.
- Hours: most placements run standard U.S. business hours on a schedule the client sets. Shifts outside standard business hours, including evenings and overnight, can be arranged on request. Pricing does not change with the shift and there is no after-hours upcharge.
- Assistants administer the back office under the client's direction. The owner still runs the business and supervises any people, and anything requiring a professional license stays with the client's licensed staff.

## Case studies
- Client video transcripts. Each video has its own page with the full transcript as text:
  - [Isaac Saldana, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/isaac-saldana-60-day-check-in): the only client video in which a replacement is described. Isaac Saldana runs Brockway Commercial, an independent commercial brokerage rather than a Keller Williams office. His first placement was a mismatch; VRA matched him again and sixty days in he calls Joel a very important part of the company, crediting the DISC and Keller Personality Assessment results for showing him how to use his assistant’s strengths. Relevant to any question about what happens when a placement does not work out.
  - [Ken Foster, 14-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/ken-foster-14-day-check-in): Ken Foster rates his virtual assistant Jerome an A+ two weeks in, and describes the calendaring, email triage and follow-up Jerome had already taken on.
  - [Ken Foster, 30-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/ken-foster-30-day-check-in): At 30 days, Ken Foster's assistant has taken the marketing effort up a level in a short period of time.
  - [Ken Foster, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/ken-foster-60-day-check-in): At 60 days, Ken Foster describes the training VRA continues to give assistants after they are placed with a client.
  - [Montse Foster, 90-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/montse-foster-90-day-check-in): After 19 years in business together and 22 years combined in the industry, Montse Foster describes the business going to the next level at her 90-day check-in.
  - [Debbie Yates, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/debbie-yates-60-day-check-in): Debbie Yates had questions about where the value would come from. Sixty days in, she answers them.
  - [Elle Haynes, 30-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/elle-haynes-30-day-check-in): Elle Haynes expected an entry-level associate. Her assistant led a full company rebrand, including the research behind the color and imagery choices.
  - [Clay Stagg, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/clay-stagg-60-day-check-in): Clay Stagg's assistant built his website and social accounts and is learning QuickBooks. Sixty days in, he says she has already paid for her first year.
  - [Rayan Saleh, 14-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/rayan-saleh-14-day-check-in): Two weeks in, Rayan Saleh of The Butcher's Grille cannot work out how he managed without an assistant.
  - [Kim Dixon-Dudley, 30-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/kim-dixon-dudley-30-day-check-in): Kim Dixon-Dudley measures her assistant against her own three Ps — and has already made a referral.
  - [Hannah DuBose, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/hannah-dubose-60-day-check-in): Hannah DuBose's assistant records every meeting and keeps her own notes, so the questions stopped coming.
  - [Emily Zakhem, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/emily-zakhem-60-day-check-in): Emily Zakhem was against the idea, tried it, went six months without one, and came back.
  - [Alexandra Pocora, check-in](https://vra.global/watch/alexandra-pocora-check-in): Alexandra Pocora works in business brokerage and commercial real estate. Her assistant is there at 8:30 every morning.
  - [Melanne Carpenter, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/melanne-carpenter-60-day-check-in): Melanne Carpenter's assistant spent month one on organization and month two on the listings. She has the most listings she has ever had.
  - [Quinton Randel, client check-in](https://vra.global/watch/quinton-randel-eidlexit-check-in): Quinton Randel runs EIDLexit, which has nothing to do with real estate, and works with ten VRA virtual assistants. He has no reservations about them speaking to his clients with minimal oversight.
  - [Brandon Lara, 90-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/brandon-lara-90-day-check-in): Brandon Lara's assistant read his KPA and understands his DISC, so she works his pain points first. He had previously spent hours training assistants and writing SOPs for them.
  - [Austin Galvez, 30-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/austin-galvez-30-day-check-in): Austin Galvez is a CPA. Thirty days in, the things that used to fall through the cracks no longer do.
  - [Courtney Okanlomo, 60-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/courtney-okanlomo-60-day-check-in): Courtney Okanlomo manages around 72 agents and a small staff, and did not believe in virtual assistants. Sixty days in, she says her assistant has revamped the entire operation.
  - [James Del Bosque, 90-day check-in](https://vra.global/watch/james-del-bosque-90-day-check-in): James Del Bosque works in mortgage. Ninety days in, his assistant Laurenz has taken complete ownership of the inbox and replies to clients and referral partners.
- [Ninety days with one virtual assistant](https://vra.global/insights/ninety-days-with-one-virtual-assistant): Ken and Montse Foster of Keller Williams Memorial filmed at all four VRA check-ins — day 14, 30, 60 and 90 — with the same assistant. Day 14 is calendar and inbox triage plus follow-up the client would otherwise have dropped; day 30 the marketing steps up; day 60 the client praises the training VRA continues after placement; day 90, after 19 years in business together, the owners describe a step change. Shows what the check-in cadence is for: each one is where the scope widens deliberately.
- [What a virtual assistant actually costs](https://vra.global/insights/virtual-assistant-cost): published industry rates run $4-$79/hour; the four ways providers obscure price (no price, "starting at", inconsistent figures, and tiers buyers cannot place themselves in), what genuinely drives the rate, and VRA’s flat $1,500/month full-time or $800/month part-time. Includes a cost FAQ.
- [Virtual assistant or first employee?](https://vra.global/insights/virtual-assistant-or-first-employee): the two options set side by side — cost, commitment, management load and what each is actually good for, for an owner making a first hire.
- [SOPs for small business](https://vra.global/insights/sops-for-small-business): how to write procedures people follow, and why an assistant is usually the one who should be writing them.
- [She already paid for her first year](https://vra.global/insights/vacation-rental-assistant-paid-for-herself): a Guadalupe River vacation rental operator's assistant built his website and social presence and took on the books within 60 days.
- [Fifteen virtual assistants, four functions](https://vra.global/insights/fifteen-virtual-assistants-outside-real-estate): a nationwide services firm runs sales, client service, marketing and HR on fifteen VRA assistants, with no real estate involved.
- [From One VA to Three: title and escrow professionals](https://vra.global/insights/title-company-virtual-assistants): A compliance leader who advises Texas title agencies grew from one VRA assistant to three and refers her own clients; plus the Qualia production work VRA assistants handle for title offices.
- [One Market Center, Ten Virtual Assistants](https://vra.global/insights/one-market-center-ten-virtual-assistants): How a single Keller Williams market center came to run ten VRA assistants across its back office.
- [14, 30, 60 and 90 days in: Keller Williams agent results](https://vra.global/insights/keller-williams-agent-14-and-60-day-results): What KW agents report at each VRA check-in milestone.
- [AI tools for real estate agents: what to use and what to delegate](https://vra.global/insights/ai-tools-for-real-estate-agents): built on primary survey data rather than assertion. NAR’s 2026 REALTORS® Technology Report (September 2026, 1,200 agents) shows AI users concentrated on writing tasks — listing descriptions 75%, social posts 56%, emails and follow-ups 52% — and at 10% or below on transaction timeline steps, client status updates, summarizing disclosures and contracts, and filling forms. Those low-adoption tasks are the ones that need access to the MLS, the CRM or the transaction file and end with something having happened rather than been written. The same split appears in title and escrow (Qualia/ALTA: 90% adoption, about 94% with no company-wide AI policy), insurance agencies (2026 Agency Universe Study: 46% using AI, top uses marketing content, coverage form analysis, contract reviews) and home services (Housecall Pro: 70% tried AI, about 40% actively using it), while Census BTOS shows 37% AI use at firms of 250+ employees against under 20% at firms of four or fewer. Carries NAR’s own guidance that AI content should not go straight from prompt to publication, with review staying the agent’s responsibility, plus a six-question FAQ.
- [Should you just use AI instead of hiring a virtual assistant?](https://vra.global/insights/ai-or-virtual-assistant): AI produces the draft; sending it, tracking the reply, entering the data, chasing the signature and following up still has to happen in the client’s own systems, and that follow-through is where an owner’s hours go. Also covers the second gap — AI answers the question it is asked, while an assistant who knows the business raises the one the owner forgot — a task-by-task table of what AI gives you versus what still has to happen, a section on what AI gets wrong (fluent whether or not it is right, what client information goes into a prompt, and the fact that accountability does not divide), what to hand to AI versus an assistant, and the fact that Claude and ChatGPT are part of the Essential Toolkit each VRA assistant completes before their first client interview, with a deeper AI track for assistants whose clients need it. Includes a five-question FAQ.
- [Breaking the growth ceiling](https://vra.global/insights/breaking-the-growth-ceiling): Operational leverage rather than headcount as the constraint on a growing business.

## Industries
- [Title and escrow](https://vra.global/title-escrow-virtual-assistant): Qualia title production, pre-closing file review support, underwriter and lender document coordination. Includes a title-specific FAQ.
- [What a title assistant does from order to close](https://vra.global/insights/title-virtual-assistant-order-to-close): the companion article to the title and escrow page, walking one file stage by stage. Opening the order and entering parties from the contract and lender instructions, logging the earnest money receipt, and sending payoff, HOA, survey and tax-certificate requests the day the order opens; ordering the search and logging the chain, vesting, liens, judgments, taxes, easements and restrictions against the file; working outstanding conditions as a dated list with an owner, a request date and a follow-up date, so a payoff letter or estate document that has gone quiet surfaces early; standing status updates to agents and lenders and underwriter correspondence kept organized; closing packages assembled against lender instructions, signings and notaries booked and rebooked; after signing, recording confirmed and logged, counties chased, final policy packages assembled and post-closing checklists worked. Examination, the commitment decision, settlement-statement figures and approval, and anything touching the escrow account stay with licensed staff — assistants have no signing or disbursing authority and do not release wires. Trained in Qualia, with SoftPro, RamQuest, ResWare and Settlor the same shape of workflow. Suggested measures in the first 60 days: days from order to close, share closing on the scheduled date, files per closer, average age of outstanding conditions, and status response time.
- [Remote title assistants and ALTA Best Practices](https://vra.global/insights/title-assistant-alta-best-practices): where a remote assistant lands in the framework, and what VRA can document for a vendor file. Vendor management is not one of the seven pillars — the seven are Licensing, Escrow Trust Accounting, Protecting NPI, Settlement Processes, Title Opinions, Insurance Coverage and Consumer Complaints — and third-party service providers sit inside Pillar 3, Protecting NPI, alongside third-party software, automated processes, APIs and add-ins, all asked to be consistent with the agency’s written information security program; the 2023 version 4.0 revisions extended screening expectations to anyone with access to NPI or information systems, service providers among them. Pillar 2 asks that escrow trust account transactions be conducted by authorized employees and that reconciliation be performed by someone with no signing or disbursing authority; VRA assistants have no signing or disbursing authority and do not release wires. What VRA can document: identity verification before placement, a police certificate from the assistant’s country of residence on request, an NDA on the client’s form whenever requested, confirmation of VRA insurance coverage, one named individual rather than a pool, and four weeks of instructor-led training before client work. Nothing here is compliance advice; assessing an agency’s own procedures is for the agency and its underwriter.
- [Commercial real estate and business brokerage](https://vra.global/commercial-real-estate-virtual-assistant): assistants placed with Keller Williams commercial agents work in CoStar for property and market data, LoopNet for listings, KW Command for contacts, tasks and documents, RealNex as the CRM, and DocuSign or Authentisign for signatures. Commercial and business brokerage clients include Melanne Carpenter and Sepideh Akhavi at Keller Williams Commercial, Alexandra Pocora in business brokerage and commercial, and Isaac Saldana at Brockway Commercial, which is independent rather than a Keller Williams office. Deal document control across long-cycle files, listing and pipeline follow-up, property and market research, administrative underwriting support, transaction coordination. Judgment, valuation and licensed work stay with the client.
- [Real estate](https://vra.global/real-estate-virtual-assistant)
- [Keller Williams agents](https://vra.global/keller-williams-agent-virtual-assistant)
- [Keller Williams market center leadership](https://vra.global/keller-williams-leadership-virtual-assistant): six seats a VRA assistant fills in a market center, not one role — MCA and accounting support, agent services, marketing and content, recruiting and retention, education and events, and leadership support. The two that slip first when staff is stretched are agent services, where the work is data entry done by someone agents walk up to with questions, and recognition, where a production award announced a week late or a list missing three names costs more than the time it would have taken. Recognition at Keller Williams Memorial runs on a calendar: monthly Cappers, Million Dollar Month, Top Agent in Market Area and South Texas Region Top Producers, quarterly Club Elite, the Fantastic Four and Top 1% producers, Luxury Division qualifications as agents reach them, and monthly Welcome New Associates. Memorial’s events include the monthly Meet and Greet Breakfast, Red Day, Family Reunion, Mega Camp, its annual Market Center Awards, and BOLD sign-up campaigns. Those names are Memorial’s. Red Day, Family Reunion, Mega Camp, BOLD, First Step, the Luxury Division and capping are Keller Williams-wide; most market centers run equivalents of the rest under their own names, and an assistant works to whatever the office already calls them. BOLD is a paid course, so sign-ups have to be earned rather than announced: a First Step session has to fill a room bigger than the market center training room in order to fill that training room for BOLD, which takes weeks of steady promotion. The argument for covering the back office is not the hours saved: culture is built by the people in the building, and paperwork is the first thing that takes them away from it.
- [Virtual MCA assistant for KW market centers](https://vra.global/kw-virtual-mca-assistant): one seat under the market center page. A Virtual MCA Assistant works for the Market Center Administrator the office already has — the MCA role itself is an in-office staff position and is not one VRA fills. Scope: CDA creation, upload and revision in KW Command with commission splits, deductions and mentor fees entered for the MCA’s review; accounts receivable outreach; monthly agent billing and office bill invoicing in AccountEdge; agent onboarding and offboarding; Command database upkeep; weekly agent-in/agent-out and monthly leadership reports. What stays in the office: review and approval, exceptions and write-offs, personnel matters, and conversations with agents about their own money. At Keller Williams Memorial one assistant handles over 400 CDAs a month and a receivables list of 60 to 75-plus agents. The other market center seats are agent services, marketing and content, recruiting and retention, education and events, and leadership support.
- [Mortgage and lending](https://vra.global/mortgage-virtual-assistant)
- [Virtual assistant for loan officers: what to hand off](https://vra.global/insights/virtual-assistant-for-loan-officers): the delegation companion to the mortgage page, argued from unit economics rather than workload. The Mortgage Bankers Association put total loan production expenses at $10,936 per loan in Q2 2026 against net production income of $973, and Freddie Mac’s cost-to-originate study found personnel is 67% of total production cost, with a $9,600 gap per loan between the top and bottom quartile of lenders. Order of delegation: the inbox first, then pipeline status updates and referral partner communication, then marketing and the back office. Licensed work stays with licensed staff. Includes how to hand work over without it returning — write the process down in the first week by observation rather than instruction, then widen by volume rather than by irritation.
- [Loan officer assistant or virtual assistant?](https://vra.global/insights/loan-officer-assistant-vs-virtual-assistant): the companion article to the mortgage page. A loan officer assistant role is two jobs in one — regulated work touching the application and the borrower’s financial details, and the coordination work around it. A virtual assistant does the second half only: inbox coverage and replies to borrowers and referral partners, pipeline tracking and status updates, scheduling, referral partner communication, CRM upkeep, marketing, invoicing and reporting. It does not do the first half: no taking applications, no collecting income, asset or credit details, no loan origination system access, no underwriting or condition-clearing. Cost comparison uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics median for loan interviewers and clerks, $50,020 a year as of May 2025, against $1,500 a month full-time or $800 part-time. Quotes James Del Bosque of GFS Home Loans on handing over inbox ownership.
- [Insurance agencies](https://vra.global/insurance-agency-virtual-assistant): certificates of insurance (COIs), renewal prep and reminders, endorsement paperwork, agency management system (AMS) data entry, client service email, scheduling and marketing support for independent agencies. No licensed work: no quoting, selling, binding or advising on coverage, which stay with the agency’s licensed staff.
- [AI tools for insurance agencies: what to use and what to delegate](https://vra.global/insights/ai-tools-for-insurance-agencies): the companion article to the insurance agency page, built on primary survey data. Liberty Mutual’s 2026 Independent Agency Growth Study (nearly 1,200 agency principals and staff) found 65% of agents had used AI on the job in the past year, up from 37%, while 14% said their agency had implemented an AI tool — and the harder measures barely moved: 29% of principals say they know enough to make AI decisions, 22% trust AI with client data, 18% have a defined AI policy. Reported time savings cluster on summarizing meeting notes (44%), marketing content (43%) and comparing policy details (34%), with routine automation such as data entry last at 26%; AI users save about four hours a week, which is time returned to an individual rather than capacity added to the service operation. The Big “I” and Future One 2026 Agency Universe Study (1,376 respondents) shows independent agencies down from about 39,000 in 2024 to about 37,000, average staff up from 8.2 to 9.9, revenue rising, and finding and screening job candidates as the top challenge at 45% — ahead of keeping up with AI at 43%. Zywave’s 2026 Broker Services Survey (1,400+ US employers) names slow response times, inconsistent communication and the broker not acting as a strategic advisor as the top reasons a client would switch brokers. The article sets out the licensed-work line — the assistant gathers quote information, no binding, no advising on coverage — and the service work an assistant takes instead: renewal runway, COIs from existing policy data, exposure information, endorsement paperwork, carrier follow-up and AMS hygiene. Includes a seven-question FAQ.
- [How commercial real estate agents use a virtual assistant](https://vra.global/insights/commercial-real-estate-virtual-assistants): the companion article to the commercial real estate page, built from two client check-ins. Melanne Carpenter, a commercial agent at KW Commercial, at 60 days: month one went on organization, month two on listing follow-up, and she reports having the most listings she has ever had with her assistant keeping the pipeline moving while she sources new business. Alexandra Pocora, in business brokerage and commercial, on document organization and marketing. The pattern both describe is that organization comes before anything visible, because an assistant working inside a disorganized system spends their time asking where things are. Commercial cycles of twelve to eighteen months mean servicing current listings and sourcing new ones compete for the same hours.
- [Sales and client service teams](https://vra.global/sales-service-teams-virtual-assistant)
- [Home services and trades](https://vra.global/home-services-virtual-assistant)
- [Hospitality: hotels, resorts, vacation rentals and event venues](https://vra.global/hospitality-virtual-assistant): guest and reservation support — booking inquiries by phone, email and chat, confirmations and change requests, group, event and venue inquiries, turnover scheduling with cleaners and maintenance, listing, rate and availability updates across booking platforms and the property’s own site, and guest follow-up and review requests. Assistants work in whichever system the property already runs — Guesty, Hostaway or OwnerRez on the rental side, Cloudbeds or the property’s own PMS for hotels and resorts, and the channels it distributes through, Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com among them. Restaurants and bars are covered on their own page rather than here.
- [Virtual assistant for vacation rentals](https://vra.global/insights/virtual-assistant-for-vacation-rentals): the companion article to the hospitality page, walking one booking through the guest cycle. The inquiry answered before the guest books elsewhere, with the calendar checked and the dates quoted; confirmations, pre-arrival details, door-code timing, guest screening where a platform or insurer requires it, and change requests; in-stay questions answered from the owner’s house guide, with leaks, lockouts and neighbor complaints escalated to whoever is on the ground; turnovers scheduled against the live calendar with photo confirmation from the cleaner; review requests, review replies drafted for approval, repeat-guest follow-up where platform terms allow, and the listing and photo maintenance nobody schedules. Pricing rules the owner sets — seasonal rates, weekend premiums, minimum stays, gap-night discounts — are executed across channels and reported on; choosing the strategy stays with the owner. Works in Guesty, Hostaway or OwnerRez and across Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com, with QuickBooks for owner statements.
- [Restaurants](https://vra.global/restaurant-virtual-assistant)
- [What a restaurant virtual assistant actually does](https://vra.global/insights/restaurant-virtual-assistant-tasks): the companion article to the restaurant page, listing the admin a restaurant hands over — reservations and guest messages, online-ordering and delivery-platform housekeeping, review replies, vendor and invoice tracking, scheduling support, menu and listing updates, and social content.
- [Virtual assistant for catering and private events](https://vra.global/insights/virtual-assistant-for-catering-and-events): the catering booking desk from first inquiry to final invoice. Inquiry inbox and web forms answered while the inquiry is warm; event details captured; proposals built from menus and pricing the business has already set; tastings booked; contracts issued and deposits chased; the event order, guest counts, allergen notes, rentals, venue load-in windows and staffing roster kept current; the week before, final counts and suppliers confirmed; afterwards the invoice, the review request and the follow-up that produces repeat business. Menu design, costing and pricing stay with the chef and owner. Works in Caterease, Tripleseat, HoneyBook, 17hats, Better Cater or a spreadsheet — whatever the business already runs. Seasonal operations move between part-time and full-time rather than waiting for a renewal date.
- [Small business](https://vra.global/small-business-virtual-assistant): the deliberate catch-all — admin, executive and office support for any industry, including those with no page here.
- [Real estate investors and landlords](https://vra.global/real-estate-investor-virtual-assistant): rentals and property management, fix-and-flip and rehab coordination, and deal back-office work.
- [Bilingual assistants — Spanish and Portuguese](https://vra.global/bilingual-virtual-assistant): for businesses whose clients and customers speak Spanish or Portuguese. The assistant handles client service email, document collection, follow-up, scheduling and phone coverage in either language, alongside the same administrative work any VRA assistant does. Coverage conversations and anything requiring a professional license stays with the client’s own licensed staff. The rate is the same as any other placement — $1,500/month full-time, $800/month part-time — with no bilingual upcharge. Book a free consult to be matched with bilingual candidates and interview them on Zoom. If the match a business needs is not open at the time, there is a [bilingual waitlist](https://vra.global/bilingual-waitlist).
- [Managing an assistant with DISC and KPA](https://vra.global/insights/managing-an-assistant-with-disc-and-kpa): what clients do with the matching assessments after the match, which almost nobody explains. VRA runs a DISC assessment and a Keller Personality Assessment on both the assistant and the client. Two directions are documented on camera: Brandon Lara’s assistant read his KPA and DISC and sequenced her week against them, working on his weak points first; Isaac Saldana of Brockway Commercial read his assistant’s results and shaped the role around what the assistant was strongest at. The assessments make a good match work faster but do not rescue a bad one, which is what the no-cost replacement is for.
- [Executive assistants](https://vra.global/executive-virtual-assistant): a role rather than an industry. An assistant assigned to one person: inbox ownership and triage, calendar, travel, meeting preparation, drafting correspondence, follow-up tracking and screening, plus the vendor, invoice, reporting and SOP work behind the role. Placed with brokers and operating principals, team leaders, title, escrow and lending principals, founders and managing partners, and professional-services principals. Most placements are in real estate, but the role is not industry-specific. Matching uses DISC and a Keller Personality Assessment, and the assistant reads the client’s. Full-time assistants work for one client exclusively.
- [Digital marketing](https://vra.global/digital-marketing-virtual-assistant)
- [Accounting and tax practices](https://vra.global/accounting-virtual-assistant): client document collection, scheduling, deadline tracking, invoicing and past-due invoice follow-up for accounting and tax firms.

## Ownership transitions
- [Preparing to sell a business](https://vra.global/selling-your-business): owner dependency and what it costs a seller — the discount, money held back, a longer stay-on, carrying part of the sale.
- [Newly acquired businesses](https://vra.global/just-bought-a-business): what to delegate in the first 90 days after buying a small business, and the cost of an assistant versus a hire.
- [Business brokers](https://vra.global/business-brokers): documenting procedures before a listing goes live so an owner-dependent business is sellable.
- [SBA lenders](https://vra.global/sba-lenders): transition risk in acquisition lending, and continuity of administration through the handover.
- [Exit planning advisors](https://vra.global/exit-planning-advisors): implementation capacity behind a readiness recommendation the owner has agreed to but has no hours to act on.
- [Your first 100 days after buying a business](https://vra.global/insights/first-100-days-after-buying-a-business): a week-by-week plan for a new owner — what to learn before changing anything, which administrative work to hand off first, and the order in which an owner stops being the bottleneck.
- [How to make a business run without you](https://vra.global/insights/how-to-make-your-business-run-without-you): owner dependency as a solvable problem — what to document, what to delegate, and what has to stay with the owner.

## Company
- [Home](https://vra.global/)
- [About VRA](https://vra.global/about): the leadership and support team by name, how assistants are screened and trained (DISC and Keller assessments, a mandatory four-week instructor-led program, 0.89% of applicants through the most recent cohort), and what VRA commits to after placement.
- [Pricing](https://vra.global/pricing)
- [How hiring works](https://vra.global/how-it-works): the two ways to start — complete the Needs Assessment online beforehand, or walk through it together on the call — then interview the matched assistants on Zoom and choose. Once selected, an assistant can start within 24 hours.
- [Software and platforms](https://vra.global/tools-and-platforms): the systems VRA assistants work in for clients today (KW Command, Qualia, Dotloop, Lone Wolf, HAR MLS, AccountEdge, BrokerKit, Courted, Mailchimp, QuickBooks, Canva, Google Workspace, Slack, Claude), plus a commitment to 90% proficiency in a client's own software within 5 business days.
